questions.question: At fixed claim rate $\lambda$, $L_t$ is the class in year $t$ and $p_{ij}(\lambda)=\mathbb{P}(L_{t+1}=j\mid L_t=i,\lambda)$. What information does entry $p_{ij}(\lambda)$ describe?
options: The current class given the next class.
The joint event of both class observations.
The next class given the current class.
The next class without conditioning on class.

questions.question: A bonus-malus model has classes $1,\ldots,m$. For fixed rate $\lambda$, $p_{ij}$ is the probability of next class $j$ given current class $i$. Why must $\sum_{j=1}^m p_{ij}=1$ for each modelled current class?
options: Exactly one next class occurs under the same condition.
Every current class has the same probability.
Every destination receives the same probability.
A class can be reached only from itself.

questions.question: For a bonus-malus cohort, $a_t=(\mathbb{P}(L_t=1),\ldots,\mathbb{P}(L_t=m))$ is the row vector of class probabilities. A transition row conditions on one current class. What distinguishes $a_t$ from a transition row?
options: It describes destinations given current class one.
It describes occupancy without fixing a current class.
It describes premiums rather than class probabilities.
It describes only the most likely current class.

questions.question: A fixed-rate bonus-malus model uses deterministic class updates, independent yearly claim counts conditional on rate $\lambda$, and the same transition matrix $P$ every year. For initial row distribution $a_0$, why does $a_t=a_0P^t$ hold?
options: Different yearly rates give the same matrix powers.
Independence makes all transition rows identical.
Each year repeats the same conditional propagation.
The initial class has no effect after one year.

questions.question: Annual reported count $N$ is Poisson with mean $1$, so $\mathbb{P}(N=n)=\mathrm{e}^{-1}/n!$. From a given class, the update goes to class $2$ exactly when $N\ge2$. What is the transition probability to class $2$?

A two-class model uses the zero-rate Poisson boundary $\mathbb{P}(N=0)=1$. Its update from class $1$ sends zero claims to class $2$ and positive counts to class $1$. What is the row of transitions from class $1$?
A two-class cohort has current row distribution $a=(0.5,0.5)$. Its transition matrix has rows $(0.8,0.2)$ and $(0.3,0.7)$, with columns ordered $1,2$. What is its next distribution $aP$?

For independent annual transitions with the same two-class matrix $P$, whose rows are $(0.8,0.2)$ and $(0.3,0.7)$, what is $(P^2)_{12}$, the probability of class $2$ after two years given initial class $1$?
A two-class transition matrix has rows $(0.8,0.2)$ and $(0.3,0.7)$. Its column sums are $1.1$ and $0.9$. Is it a valid transition matrix under the row convention?
options: No; each column must also sum to one.
Yes; rows are non-negative and sum to one.
No; each row must contain equal entries.
Yes; column totals alone establish validity.

questions.question: A two-class transition matrix has rows $(0.8,0.2)$ and $(0.3,0.7)$. The class names are swapped consistently: old class $2$ becomes new class $1$. What are the new matrix rows, with both indices using the new names?

For a sufficient bonus-malus class state, the first year uses transition matrix $P_0$ and the second uses $P_1$. Both follow the row convention. Which expression gives the two-year distribution from row $a_0$ for every such pair of matrices?

A discount requires two consecutive claim-free years. States $G,P,I$ mean a claim in the latest year, one clean year since a claim, and at least two clean years. Next annual count $N$ satisfies $0<\mathbb{P}(N=0)<1$. Under the yearly history update, what is the one-year transition probability from $G$ to $I$?
options: $\mathbb{P}(N=0)$.
$\mathbb{P}(N=0)^2$.
$\mathbb{P}(N\ge1)$.

questions.question: A driver starts in class $1$ and has next-class probabilities $0.6$ and $0.4$ for classes $1$ and $2$. The premium at class label $l$ is $100l^2$. What is the expected next-year premium?
A cohort has current probabilities $(0.5,0.5)$ and transition rows $(0.8,0.2)$ and $(0.3,0.7)$. What is the probability of previous class $1$ conditional on observing next class $2$?

Each driver has fixed unobserved annual claim probability $r$, equal to $1/2$ or $1/4$ with equal prior probabilities. Years are independent conditional on $r$. Let $L_t=0$ mean year $t$ was claim-free and $L_t=1$ mean it had a claim. For current $L_2=0$, compare histories $(L_1,L_2)=(0,0)$ and $(1,0)$. Must their next-claim probabilities agree?
options: Yes; conditional yearly independence removes the latent rate.
Yes; the same current class forces the same predictive law.
No; the histories give different weights to the two rates.
No; conditional independence fails for each driver.

questions.question: A two-class cohort starts with row distribution $a=(1,0)$ and after one year has $b=(0.6,0.4)$. Its unknown transition matrix $P$ follows the row convention. What does $aP=b$ identify about the second row?
options: Any $(x,1-x)$ with $0\le x\le1$ remains possible.
It must equal the first row $(0.6,0.4)$.
It must be $(0.4,0.6)$ to balance columns.
It must be $(0,1)$ because class $2$ starts empty.

questions.question: A two-class cohort has current probabilities $(0.5,0.5)$. The probability of moving from class $2$ to class $2$ is $0.8$, while that from class $1$ to class $2$ is unknown $x$. Can a valid transition matrix give next-class $2$ probability $0.3$?
options: Yes; choosing $x=-0.2$ gives the target.
No; the attainable probability is at least $0.4$.
Yes; choosing $x=0.2$ gives the target.
Yes; choosing $x=0.6$ gives the target.

questions.question: A two-year claim-free discount has high-price history states $G$ (latest year had a claim) and $P$ (one clean year since a claim). A clean next year, with probability $0.8$, sends $P$ to the low-price state but leaves $G$ high. Within the high-price group, cohort A has 75% $G$ and cohort B has 25% $G$. What prevents one high/low transition matrix from describing both cohorts?
options: Their high-to-low probabilities are both 0.8.
Their high-to-low probabilities are both zero.
Their high-to-low probabilities are 0.6 and 0.2.
Their high-to-low probabilities are 0.2 and 0.6.

questions.question: There are $m\ge2$ classes. Let $\boldsymbol{a}_t$ be the row vector of current class probabilities and let $\boldsymbol{P}$ have current classes in rows and next classes in columns. Which identity gives the next row vector for every such transition matrix and current distribution?
options: $\boldsymbol{a}_{t+1}=\boldsymbol{P}\boldsymbol{a}_t$
$\boldsymbol{a}_{t+1}=\boldsymbol{a}_t\boldsymbol{P}^{\top}$
$\boldsymbol{a}_{t+1}=\boldsymbol{a}_t+\boldsymbol{P}$
$\boldsymbol{a}_{t+1}=\boldsymbol{a}_t\boldsymbol{P}$
